target.title: EU refunds are a cent off
target.description: Support ticket #4471. Customers paying in EUR or GBP get partial refunds that differ by one cent from their share of what they paid. Example: an order of 10.07 EUR for 3 units, refunding 1 unit, returns 3.35 EUR instead of 3.36 EUR. Finance noticed it in the monthly reconciliation; about 2% of EU refunds are affected. Expected: the customer gets back exactly their share, rounded half-even to the cent, in their own currency. Do not change how payments are settled with the processor (USD).
comments: Reproduced locally with order 10.07 EUR / 3 units / refund 1: got 3.35, expected 3.36. USD orders are fine.
Checked refunds/calc.py prorate(): it rounds half-even correctly on its own, so the rounding rule itself is not the bug.
Tried switching prorate() to ROUND_HALF_UP: fixes the GBP case but breaks test_refund_rounding and the EUR cases still fail. Reverted.
Tried raising FX rate precision from 4 to 8 places in payments/fx.py: breaks receipts (test_fx expects 4 places, finance requires it). Reverted.
refunds/service.py converts the order total to USD, prorates in USD, then converts back to the order currency. Two roundings plus a 4-place FX rate lose a cent.
Flipping settings.SETTLE_IN_USD to False makes refunds right but breaks settlement (test_settlement); finance reconciles in USD, so that is not allowed.
Plan: compute the customer's refund share in the order currency (no round trip); only convert to USD where the processor needs it.
Paused here: no code changes yet. Next session should implement the plan and add a test for the 10.07 EUR case.
